correctness.rationale: For S(n)=prod(j!,1<=j<=n), Legendre excludes precisely odd valuation with odd-unit 7 modulo 8 when the 2-adic valuation is even. Pairing binary digit sums shows that odd n are excluded exactly when n=5 mod 8; for n=2m, the obstruction is even s_2(m) and f(m)=7 mod 8. The factorial odd-unit recurrences f(2t)=f(t)O(t), f(2t+1)=f(t)O(t)(2t+1) derive the local binary parities A(m),B(m). The explicit 32-state deterministic bit automaton carries (m mod4,s_2(m) mod2,f(m) mod8), has constant row/column sum 2, a primitive Perron 2 eigenvalue and verified annihilating polynomial with remaining nonzero roots on |z|=sqrt(2); the dyadic-cylinder decomposition gives E(X)=3X/16+O(sqrt X). Cayley-Hamilton applied to diag(M^8,256,16) proves E(2^(8j+5))=3*2^(8j+1)+2^(4j) for every j >=0 from 34 exact initial equalities, not from extrapolation. Independently recomputed the odd-unit/valuation test for n=0..599 (first obstructions 5,10,13,20,21,24,29,37,45,48,53,61), the annihilator and small cylinder counts. These are corroborations of the unrestricted symbolic proof.
